concepts.definition: A sprite moving towards a target sprite at a fixed speed, every frame.
concepts.example: The ghost follows the cat at speed 25 and turns whichever way the cat goes.
concepts.pitfall: Putting the same sprite in both slots: the sprite tries to follow itself and does not move at all.

concepts.definition: How far apart the centres of two sprites are, in pixels.
concepts.example: If the centres are 60 pixels apart sideways and 80 pixels apart up-down, the distance is 100.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking only the sideways difference is the distance; the up-down difference counts too.

concepts.definition: The largest distance at which the enemy notices the player; in the rule it is written as the number in a comparison.
concepts.example: If the distance is less than 70, the ghost chases; otherwise it stops.
concepts.pitfall: Choosing a threshold that is too big: the ghost sees you from everywhere and the game becomes unfairly hard.

concepts.definition: stops sets the speed to zero and ends the following; stops following only ends the following and leaves the speed as it is.
concepts.example: If stops following is used, the ghost keeps sliding at its last speed.
concepts.pitfall: Using stops following where it should stop: the ghost slides as if it were on ice.

concepts.definition: An event that runs 60 times a second while the game is on; used for rules that must be checked all the time.
concepts.example: A ghost that measures the distance every frame notices at once when the cat comes near.
concepts.pitfall: Putting the distance check inside when game starts: it is checked once and never tested again.

quiz.prompt: The ghost's centre is at (20, 30) and the cat's centre is at (80, 110). What does the distance block give?
quiz.explanation: The sideways difference is 80 - 20 = 60, the up-down difference is 110 - 30 = 80. Distance = square root(60 x 60 + 80 x 80) = square root(10000) = 100. Adding the differences to get 140 is wrong; the distance is the diagonal line.

quiz.prompt: The cat is standing still. The ghost wakes up 70 pixels from the cat and follows at speed 25. How many seconds pass until the distance drops to 20 pixels?
quiz.explanation: The gap to close is 70 - 20 = 50 pixels. Time = distance / speed = 50 / 25 = 2 seconds. Because following moves in a straight line at a fixed speed, the calculation is direct.

quiz.prompt:
The program is:

```
every frame:
  if distance(hayalet, kedi) < 70 do
    hayalet follows kedi at speed 25
  else
    hayalet stops following
```

The cat comes near the ghost, and the ghost wakes up and chases. Then the cat moves away fast and the distance goes past 70. What does the ghost do?
options: It goes back to where it started
It keeps sliding in the same direction at its last speed
quiz.explanation: "Stops following" only breaks the follow link; the speed stays as it is. The ghost keeps going in its current direction at speed 25. To make it stop, "stops" should have been put in the else branch.

quiz.prompt:
The ghost does not move at all. Which is the bug?

```
every frame:
  hayalet follows sprite hayalet at speed 25
```
options: The follow speed should not be 25
The every frame event cannot be used for following
The ghost is also chosen as the target; the ghost is following itself
The ghost should not be of the Enemy kind
quiz.explanation: The same sprite has been put in both slots of the follow block. A sprite cannot follow itself, so the block does nothing. The cat should have been put in the second slot. The speed and the event choice are correct.

quiz.prompt: Why do we write the distance check inside "every frame" instead of "when game starts"?
options: The distance changes as the cat moves; the rule must be tested again 60 times a second
The when game starts event does not support the distance block
Every frame takes up less space
The follow block only works inside every frame
quiz.explanation: The when game starts block runs only once; if the cat comes near later, nobody checks again. The every frame event runs 60 times a second, so the ghost notices at once when the cat comes near. When game starts can use the distance block too; the problem is the timing.
